## Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**Top pick: JBL Charge 6.** It has an IP68 rating, which both What Hi-Fi and iTechGuides call the highest protection among the picks they compared. Battery life is 20 hours (28 with Playtime Boost) per [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart), and Best Products lists 28 hours as its maximum ([Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)). It also doubles as a power bank. Prices in the sources ranged from $129.99 to $150 (checked June and July 2026). Buy it on [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=JBL+Charge+6) or [Walmart](https://www.walmart.com/search?q=JBL+Charge+6).

**Other good options:**

- **JBL Boombox 4 (best if you want a floating speaker that handles immersion well).** RTINGS calls it its top waterproof pick. It's protected for long periods of immersion, floats, and lasts over 40 hours. The downside is narrow directivity, so it sounds muffled from the sides or behind. It's also large and heavy. See [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth).
- **Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM (best mid-range).** It has a 360-degree design, floats, and survives accidental drops and temporary immersion. Battery life is about 15 hours. See [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) and [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers). Search for it on [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Ultimate+Ears+EPICBOOM).
- **Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4 (best budget).** It's IP67, floats, and is rugged enough for drops. Battery life is about 13–14 hours. Best Products listed it at $65, down from $80 ([Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)). Search for it on [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Ultimate+Ears+WONDERBOOM+4).
- **JBL Grip (best if you want something light for the beach).** It's a can-shaped speaker with an IP68 rating, 12-hour battery, and weighs 0.85 lb. It sells for $100. See [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/).
- **Soundcore Boom 2 Plus (louder, floats, but heavy).** It's IPX7 and floats, with up to 20 hours at half volume. It weighs 3.8 kg. Dealectric lists it at $249.99 and reports a code (AFSC20) that took $49.99 off on 2026-10-22, expiring 2026-12-31. The store's checkout has the final say. [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus). Dealectric is an affiliate site and earns a commission if you buy through that link, at no extra cost to you ([source](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-boom-2-plus)).

## Keeping it working near water

- **IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine.** RTINGS notes that these ratings only measure water penetration and that frequent exposure to salt or chlorine can degrade the surface over time, especially on fabric. Rinse it with fresh water after use.
- **Protect it from sand.** Keep it on a towel or a raised surface, and make sure any flaps or port covers are closed before it gets wet.
- **Dry it before charging.** Let the exterior and the charging port dry fully before you plug it in.
- **Check the manufacturer's rules.** Some manuals advise against beach or pool use. Follow the manual for your model.

Prices and availability change, so check the retailer before buying.
